_comment: Valuation model parameters. Bump model_version whenever a formula or default changes so stored trades/values remain comparable. Every parameter is documented in docs/VALUATION_MODEL.md, docs/DYNASTY_MODEL.md and docs/ROOKIE_PICK_MODEL.md.

scale._comment: Values = points x factor. factor = anchor_value / mean(score of the top anchor_top_n reference-league assets); anchor_value null = 0.7 x top_value, which puts the top asset near 10,000. Anchoring on a top-N mean (not the single top asset) keeps every player monotone in his own inputs. The same factor is applied to the user league so values are comparable across settings.

phase._comment: Weights move linearly from the preseason set (week<=1) to the in-season set (week>=full_in_season_week).

redraft._adp_comment: ADP is a corroborating signal only: a player whose only usable signal is ADP gets no redraft value (N/A). Long ADP lists rank undrafted/out-of-league players by placeholder or stale draft positions (model 2.1.0, handoff bug #1).

outcome_range._comment: Model 2.3.0 (audit E10), display only. Columns: [projected points per game from, then realised / projected at the 10th, 25th, 75th, 90th percentile]. From the app's blend vs realised points: preseason seasons 2021-2025 and in-season checkpoints (weeks 4-12) 2021-2024, 4,719 player-windows. The +/- under a value is source disagreement (median 5.5% of value historically, containing only 13% of season outcomes); this is the range real outcomes fell in.

availability_shape._comment: Model 2.3.0 (audit E11). Stars miss fewer games than depth players, and healthy-season projections (17 games) ignore that. A missed game costs the player's surplus that week (the replacement plays), so redraft value x= share of games played at the player's positional rank RELATIVE to the position's starters (1.0 = an average starter; only the within-position shape, cross-position balance unchanged). Linear between knots (positional rank, factor), flat beyond the last knot: deeper than 2x 12-team starters, not playing is a backup's role, which projections already price in. Fitted on nflverse 2019-2025 (preseason ECR rank and in-season ROS ECR rank, weeks 1/5/9); walk-forward: historical trade outcomes 0.549 -> 0.552 (better in 5/5 seasons), lineup-value tier loss 0.033 -> 0.018 preseason, 0.806 -> 0.690 from week 9. Position-level (absolute) availability made trades worse (0.541). K/DEF: none.

production._comment: Production rate = (gp*blend + k*prior)/(gp+k), blend = (1-xfp_blend)*ppg + xfp_blend*xppg; ROS points = rate * remaining games * availability (* SoS if sos_strength > 0). k, xfp_blend fitted walk-forward (audit E2); availability = realized share of remaining team games played (E2). SoS strength 0 since 2.2.0: without it the in-season production forecast was at least as accurate in 17 of 20 walk-forward checkpoints (E2), and the projections it is blended with already include matchups (double counting). Players without a last-season rate (>=4 games) need min_games_without_history games before production is used, and regress to the positional MEDIAN.

trend._comment: v2: 30-day market trend is display-only (no evidence it predicts outcomes; it is already in the market level).

uncertainty._comment: Uncertainty per remaining game used for the option value in expected surplus E[max(0, X - r)] (+ bench band). 2.2.0: 0.4 x the 2.1.x table (which was the total forecast-error SD incl. missed games and week-to-week noise, calibrated against a hindsight target). Against hindsight-free lineup value (audit E5: weekly starts decided before each week, 2020-2025) the 2.1.x sigma over-valued ranks 13-72 relative to the top 12 by 24-57% preseason and up to 2-4x deep in season; 0.4x was best preseason (tier ratios 0.95-1.14), much better in season, and in a historical league simulation (E6, 5,000 trades) it predicted realised trade outcomes better than 1.0x in all 5 seasons. Only the option value of a player's persistent rate is real; unforeseeable weekly noise and missed games are not.

redraft._weights_comment: v2 (audit E1/E2): expert consensus was the most accurate single signal at every checkpoint and the fitted consensus weight did not decline during the season, so consensus dominates and production gets a small in-season weight. Projection/market weights are judgment (no free historical archives to backtest them).

default_aging_curves._comment: Fallback relative-PPG multipliers by age (peak = 1.0). Replaced by config/calibration/aging-curves.json when present (run `npm run calibrate`).

default_attrition._comment: Annual probability of dropping out of fantasy relevance = base + slope*max(0, age-onset), capped at 0.9. Replaced by calibration when present.

dynasty._injury_comment: 2.2.0: dynasty injuries use redraft.injury_games_lost (expected games missed) as a share of the remaining current season, and a player on IR/PUP/NFI/Suspended with no rest-of-season projection loses the whole remaining season (as in redraft). The former flat injury_year1_fraction (IR = 35% of a full season, whatever the week) was removed.
dynasty._aging_power_comment: mu_t = mu_1 * (A(age_t)/A(age_0))^aging_power. Delta-method curves understate decline (survivorship); power 2 removed the fundamental model age bias in walk-forward tests (audit E3).
dynasty._evidence_comment: Players past their first career year need current evidence (projection, current or last-season production) for a fundamental value; the draft-capital prior alone no longer values retired/out-of-league veterans.
dynasty._weights_comment: v2 (audit E3): dynasty consensus alone (rho .581) beat the fundamental model (.502); a 75/25 consensus/fundamental blend was best (.583). ADP is a near-duplicate of consensus (rho .96) and gets 0.

picks._switch_comment: From this calendar month on, the 'upcoming' rookie class is next calendar year's.
picks._prior_class_comment: When the rookie class used for the current-class/historical curves is an already-drafted class (e.g. 2026 rookies used to price 2027 picks), its values are partly 'resolved' (landing spots, early production) and ordered by today's rankings, which favours players who already hit. This multiplier removes that optimism. Market data typically prices the upcoming class's early 1st at ~0.65-0.8x the prior class's 1.01-1.04.

source_weights._comment: Relative weight of each source WITHIN a signal group. Rationale in docs/VALUATION_MODEL.md §Source weighting.
source_weights._dp_comment: DynastyProcess player values are a transform of FantasyPros ECR (within-position rho .99): counting them as an independent market double-counts consensus. Kept for display; weight 0. DP pick values are kept (no duplicate pick consensus exists).

mapping._comment: A ranking/market list must contain at least this many matched players at a position to be mapped onto that position's value curve.

trade_outcome._dynasty_comment: Model 2.4.0 (audit E15): P(the side receiving more dynasty value ends the next three seasons with more lineup points, discounted 0.82 a year) = 1 / (1 + exp(-slope x |margin|)). Fitted on 2 x 5,000 random player trades in 12-team dynasty leagues replayed on real 2020-2025 weekly points (preseason dynasty ECR + fundamental values, 20-man rosters): slope 1.75 on both seeds, 1.5-2.0 in every start season; margins under 20% came out ahead 46-56% of the time, 30-50% 67-69%, 75%+ 81%. Draft picks are not in the simulation (no historical pick values): pick trades use the same curve. Remove it to return dynasty to the z-score levels.
trade_outcome._roster_comment: Model 2.3.0 (audit E12), display only (My Team): P(a team's season points rose) = 1 / (1 + exp(-k x |change in expected lineup points per week|)). From 10,000 team-trades in the historical league simulations: +1 / +3 points per week -> 55% / 65%; 4+ -> 81% observed. Realised gain = 0.80 x predicted.
trade_outcome._levels_comment: Model 2.3.0 (audit E10): redraft verdict levels come from the same historical frequency: close < 60% (margin under ~27%), lean 60-70%, clear >= 70% (margin >= ~56%). Historically margins under 30% won 53-57% whatever their size, 30-50% won 64%, 50-75% 72%, 75%+ 80%. The z-score levels (|diff| / the +/- range) disagreed with the frequency shown under the verdict in 23% of trades. Since 2.4.0 dynasty uses the same levels on its own calibrated frequency (dynasty_logit_slope, audit E15: close < 60% = margin under ~17%, lean 17-42%, clear >= ~42%; favoured side won 51% / 64% / 77%). Remove 'levels' to use z in both modes.
trade_outcome._comment: P(the side receiving more value ends the season with more lineup points) = 1 / (1 + exp(-slope x |margin|)), margin = difference / larger side. Fitted on 5,000 random trades in historical league simulations (audit E7: 12-team PPR, full seasons 2020-2025, real weekly points): margins of 10% / 30% / 50% came out ahead 54% / 61% / 68% of the time. Shown next to the verdict; it does not change any value. Dynasty: dynasty_logit_slope (2.4.0, audit E15).

package._comment: Extra players received in an uneven trade are charged lineup displacement (surplus of the average team's worst starter at that position × strength) and a roster-slot cost (value of the last rostered player). Picks are exempt from both.
